items.title: Albert Nicholas Interview, 1967-02-09
items.q: Jelly, he's my favorite... But you had to know him, you know. If you met him the first time... He was truthful... I've seen him at the rhythm club in New York... I've seen him ask Duke, come on and sit down and play a little bit.

ctx.x: Going back to the old days for a moment, would you like to tell us a bit about Jelly Roll more?

Well, Jelly, he's my favorite. Jelly Roll was something else. He was a character. A lot of people, youngsters ask me about Jelly Roll. They got the wrong impression of Jelly, I think. Jelly was a great musician and a great person, but you had to know him, you know. If you met him the first time, you might think he was very arrogant, because he did speak what he thought. You know, he was outspoken. But one thing I'll say about Jelly, he spoke the truth. Whatever he said, he meant it. He was truthful. And if you…

Oh, he did. But don't you think he suffered because he couldn't adapt himself to playing in the 30s? His style was so rigid. Huh? His style was so rigid that he couldn't fit into the music of the 30s.
